title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
This incident shows impersonation enabled by AI-generated video and social media accounts. Scammers created deepfake videos of a real immigration attorney and fake profiles across multiple platforms to solicit payment from vulnerable immigrants for services never offered. The deployment failure occurred entirely outside any legitimate system: the AI tools were used to manufacture false identity and credibility in an uncontrolled criminal operation.

What would have caught this was not better AI design but platform enforcement. Social media companies' detection systems failed to identify and prevent the creation of thousands of fraudulent accounts before an attorney had to hire external anti-piracy services to remove them. The scam relied on the platforms' inability or unwillingness to verify accounts claiming professional credentials.

It is not established whether the individuals running the scam built or trained their own generative models, or merely used existing commercial AI tools to create the deepfakes. The financial and operational details of the criminal network remain unknown.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of artificial intelligence scammers who are using deepfake videos and fake social media profiles to defraud vulnerable immigrants. The criminals create AI-generated content showing Leal offering immigration services he never provides, typically charging fees of around $2,200 for services like US residency assistance. The scams escalated dramatically over the past three months, prompting Leal's office to hire an anti-piracy company that has successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake accounts, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram.

The fraudulent scheme typically begins with social media videos directing potential victims to contact a phone number through WhatsApp, where scammers send phony contracts and request payment through digital payment apps like Venmo or Zelle. Leal has warned immigrants to be cautious of online services demanding upfront payment and to verify anyone offering legal assistance. He plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to investigate the scams and has already changed his personal phone number in response to the situation.
